paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Peter shows up with a number, and Jesus answers with a story about a king and two debts. One debt is ten thousand talents, the other a hundred denarii. Forgiving is never about counting, because the whole point is how much you were forgiven first (Matthew 18:22-24, 28).

Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. The master's mercy wasn't a small favor, it was a debt of ten thousand talents forgiven (Matthew 18:24, 27). When you keep that in front of you, a hundred denarii looks a whole lot smaller (Matthew 18:28). I know a little about a second chance I never saw coming, since an angel called me out of a junk drawer, and after that I can't hold a grudge over a crumb.

So the master asks the question that settles it: "Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?" (Matthew 18:33). Jesus closes by saying His heavenly Father will treat each of you that way unless you forgive your brother "from your heart" (Matthew 18:35). That means the forgiveness you've received is the reason you forgive, so go hand some out, baker. The teaching on humility and forgiveness ends here, and the Lord's mercy to you is what makes it possible.
